articles.title: Your Website Is Slow: 6 Things Worth Checking Before Blaming Your Code
articles.excerpt: Before spending hours refactoring clean code, run through this infrastructure checklist first. More often than not, the real culprits behind sluggish load times live further down the stack. High Serve…
articles.body: Every developer has been there: PageSpeed Insights is throwing red scores, Lighthouse is warning about high TTFB, and your immediate instinct is to crack open your codebase. You start profiling component renders, ripping out utility libraries, and hunting for micro-optimizations. Before spending hours refactoring clean code, run through this infrastructure checklist first. More often than not, the real culprits behind sluggish load times live further down the stack. High Server Response Time (TTFB) If a browser spends 800ms+ waiting for the first byte of HTML, frontend optimizations won't fix the lag. Check your Time to First Byte (TTFB) in the browser's Network tab or test it directly in your terminal. If it is high, the server is stalling before returning data.

articles.body: I wanted to see how close I could get to the feel of Worms Armageddon in a browser, so I built Worms.js. It has Bazooka and Grenade, destructible terrain, wind, explosions, knockback, and fall damage. You can play against a bot, share a keyboard in hot-seat mode, or invite a friend to an online match through a link. It’s built with TypeScript, React, Three.js, and React Three Fiber. Online play uses WebRTC, with Cloudflare handling lobbies and connection fallback. It’s a small, free fan project. There’s no sound, and only two weapons so far, but I’ve tried to make the movement, aiming, and physics feel close to the original. Play in your browser

articles.body: La brecha de datos en Dinamarca, con datos expuestos en el registro central, dejó al descubierto la información personal de 8,8 millones de ciudadanos mediante un ataque automatizado que abusó del acceso legítimo de una empresa privada. Ocurrió en silencio durante semanas. El servidor central que gestiona el padrón nacional danés no sufrió una intrusión directa en su base de datos. Los atacantes utilizaron credenciales corporativas válidas para consultar el sistema millones de veces sin activar las alarmas de inmediato. La información confirmada por el informe del incidente publicado en eSecurityPlanet detalla que las autoridades detectaron patrones anómalos el 2 de octubre, aunque los rastreos automatizados operaron a lo largo de septiembre.

articles.title: How to Build Financial Dashboard Pagination with Traceable Retrieval Contracts
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use staged retrieval with an explicit collection, bounded queries, and a cursor that carries source context forward. For a financial research dashboard, pagination is part of the evidenc…
articles.body: Short answer: use staged retrieval with an explicit collection, bounded queries, and a cursor that carries source context forward. For a financial research dashboard, pagination is part of the evidence contract, not a cosmetic control. The user-visible answer is usually a table of filings, a list of comparable companies, or a handful of cited passages. That output should map to a retrieval unit before any index is chosen. I write down the unit (one paragraph, one table row, or one filing section), the metadata filters (ticker, period, document type), and the freshness target. Then ingestion, querying, and citation become three observable stages. Step 1: Define the retrieval contract Start with a small, boring schema.

articles.body: In December 2025 I shipped a small CLI called Context Bank . The idea was simple and, I still think, right: keep your AI coding agent's project memory in the repo, in plain markdown under .ai/ , committed to git. articles.title: How to Monitor Your Competitors' Ads Automatically (Google, LinkedIn and Bing) with Apify
articles.excerpt: When a competitor launches a new offer, you usually see it in their ads first: a new headline, a new landing page, a new video, a webinar promo. You can watch for these yourself, because Google, Linke…
articles.body: When a competitor launches a new offer, you usually see it in their ads first: a new headline, a new landing page, a new video, a webinar promo. You can watch for these yourself, because Google, LinkedIn and Microsoft all publish public ad libraries that show who is advertising and what they are running. What these libraries don't give you is a way to say "tell me when something new shows up." This tutorial covers how to turn them into an automated feed of new competitor ads, delivered to Slack or email every morning, plus how to pull the same data with Python and analyze it with pandas.

articles.title: Open-Source Wi-Fi Vulnerability Tool Seeks Community Feedback for Ethical and Effective Improvements
articles.excerpt: Introduction: The Rise of CyclePatrol As Wi-Fi networks proliferate in public spaces, the development of CyclePatrol exemplifies the cybersecurity community’s dual imperative: to innovate while uphold…
articles.body: Introduction: The Rise of CyclePatrol As Wi-Fi networks proliferate in public spaces, the development of CyclePatrol exemplifies the cybersecurity community’s dual imperative: to innovate while upholding ethical standards. Designed as an open-source Bash tool for Kali Linux and NetHunter , CyclePatrol systematically identifies Wi-Fi vulnerabilities during field walks . Its creator, leveraging expertise in ethical hacking, engineered the tool to scan networks cyclically, assess weaknesses in protocols such as WPS , WPA2/WPA3 , and PMF , and generate detailed reports. The integration of a custom-built Cyberphone with an external antenna underscores its practical utility, enabling precise vulnerability detection in real-world environments.
